title: Halting with a specified answer
statement: Let $A$ be a memory-machine program, let an oracle assign a Boolean answer to each of $d$ deciders and each bit string, and fix an input bit string $x$. The machine halts with answer $b$ from configuration $a$ while maintaining a predicate $G$ if there is a natural number $T$ such that after $T$ steps its control state is absent, its stored result is $b$, and $G$ holds at every configuration at times $t<T$.
hypotheses_covered: $A$ maps control states to memory-machine instructions
the oracle maps a decider index and bit string to a Boolean
